topics.label: Course Introduction and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the cancer biology lecture series, the interdisciplinary audience, and the specific learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer as a Failure of Differentiation and In Vitro Study Models
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as a multi-step genetic and epigenetic breakdown of normal cellular differentiation and tissue architecture, alongside experimental models used to study tumor cells in vitro.

topics.label: Invasion, Metastasis, and Histological Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the biological processes of invasion and metastasis and illustrate how benign and malignant lesions are identified histologically, using the colorectal adenoma-to-carcinoma sequence as a model.

topics.label: Tumor Nomenclature and Mechanisms of Disease and Mortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the naming conventions for different tumor types and describe the pathophysiological mechanisms by which benign and malignant tumors cause illness and death.

topics.label: Patterns of Cancer Incidence Across Tissues and Species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the incidence and mortality rates of different tumor types in humans and across diverse animal taxa.

topics.label: Principles, Applications, and Limitations of Cancer Screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical rationale for early cancer detection and evaluate the effectiveness and limitations of screening programs across different anatomical sites.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Practical Preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by referencing the learning outcomes and providing housekeeping details for upcoming practical sessions.
